Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 104, verses 1–9:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Woe to every scorer and mocker﴾: a word by which punishment is sought; and it is a valley in Hellfire. Al-Humazah is one who frequently scorns and defames, and likewise al-Lumazah; they are those who backbite and expose the faults of others in order to corrupt.

﴿Who collects wealth and counts it﴾: that is, he counts it and prepares it for the calamities of time.

﴿He thinks his wealth will make him immortal﴾: that is, he thinks it will make him abide in life and never die.

﴿No!﴾: that is, the matter is not as he claims and supposes.

﴿He will surely be thrown﴾: that is, he will surely be cast into al-Hutamah.

﴿Into al-Hutamah﴾: that is, the Fire that crushes everything thrown into it.

﴿It rises over the hearts﴾: that is, it looks down upon the hearts and burns them.

﴿Closed over them﴾: that is, shut and sealed.

﴿In extended columns﴾: that is, they are tormented in the Fire by extended pillars.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Woe to every scorer and mocker﴾, threaten, by the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, a valley in Hellfire that flows with the pus and discharge of the people of the Fire, for every scorer and mocker, that is, every backbiter and fault-finder, of those who walk about with tale-bearing and seek to expose the defects of others.

His words, ﴿Who collects wealth and counts it, thinking his wealth will make him immortal﴾: this is another description of that scorer and mocker, namely that he ﴿collects wealth﴾, much of it from both unlawful and lawful sources, ﴿and counts it﴾, that is, he takes account of it, knows its quantity, and prepares it for the calamities of time, as he claims. ﴿He thinks his wealth will make him immortal﴾, that is, he supposes that because of the abundance of his riches he will not die. And when has wealth ever saved anyone from death? It is the delusion of life. Had wealth been able to make anyone immortal, Qarun would have been made immortal.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿No!﴾: his wealth will not make him immortal; rather, by My might and My majesty, ﴿he will surely be thrown﴾, that is, cast down, ﴿into al-Hutamah﴾, the blazing Fire that crushes everything thrown into it.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿And what will make you know what al-Hutamah is?﴾: this question is for magnifying its matter and emphasizing the gravity of its state. He, the Exalted, explained it with His words, ﴿It is the Fire of Allah, kindled, ﴾ that is, blazing and roaring, ﴿which rises over the hearts﴾, that is, looks down upon the hearts and burns them.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed it is closed over them﴾: that is, the Fire is shut and sealed over those scorers and mockers, its gates locked.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿In extended columns﴾: that is, they are tormented in the Fire by extended pillars. And Allah knows best how their torment by it will be, since Allah, the Exalted, has not informed us of its manner.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense.

2- Warning against backbiting and tale-bearing.

3- Condemnation of those deluded by wealth and impressed by it.

4- Explanation of the severity and horror of the punishment of the Fire.

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Woe to every scorer and mocker﴾, threaten, by the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, a valley in Hellfire that flows with the pus and discharge of the people of the Fire, for every scorer and mocker, that is, every backbiter and fault-finder, of those who walk about with tale-bearing and seek to expose the defects of others.

His words, ﴿Who collects wealth and counts it, thinking his wealth will make him immortal﴾: this is another description of that scorer and mocker, namely that he ﴿collects wealth﴾, much of it from both unlawful and lawful sources, ﴿and counts it﴾, that is, he takes account of it, knows its quantity, and prepares it for the calamities of time, as he claims. ﴿He thinks his wealth will make him immortal﴾, that is, he supposes that because of the abundance of his riches he will not die. And when has wealth ever saved anyone from death? It is the delusion of life. Had wealth been able to make anyone immortal, Qarun would have been made immortal.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿No!﴾: his wealth will not make him immortal; rather, by My might and My majesty, ﴿he will surely be thrown﴾, that is, cast down, ﴿into al-Hutamah﴾, the blazing Fire that crushes everything thrown into it.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿And what will make you know what al-Hutamah is?﴾: this question is for magnifying its matter and emphasizing the gravity of its state. He, the Exalted, explained it with His words, ﴿It is the Fire of Allah, kindled, ﴾ that is, blazing and roaring, ﴿which rises over the hearts﴾, that is, looks down upon the hearts and burns them.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed it is closed over them﴾: that is, the Fire is shut and sealed over those scorers and mockers, its gates locked.

His words, the Exalted, ﴿In extended columns﴾: that is, they are tormented in the Fire by extended pillars. And Allah knows best how their torment by it will be, since Allah, the Exalted, has not informed us of its manner.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense.

2- Warning against backbiting and tale-bearing.

3- Condemnation of those deluded by wealth and impressed by it.

4- Explanation of the severity and horror of the punishment of the Fire.
